source_metadata.title: CCL5 Levels, Disease Progression, and Mortality in Respiratory Viral Infections: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
source_metadata.source_type: systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies

consistency_findings.finding: The main article reports 11 studies/1214 participants for unfavorable disease progression, while Supplement 1 eTable reports 11 studies/n=1241 for the same pooled OR 0.78 (95% CI 0.71-0.85).
consistency_findings.handling: Both values were preserved as reported. No silent repair was made. Table 2 subgroup counts (609+605) sum to 1214, which supports—but does not prove—the inference that 1241 may be a supplement typographical error.

consistency_findings.finding: The Study Quality Assessment text refers to eFigure/eTable material as being in Supplement 2, while the article backmatter and supplied companion PDF place the eTable/eFigure in Supplement 1; Supplement 2 is listed as the Data Sharing Statement.
consistency_findings.handling: The companion material was identified by its actual supplied content and labeled Supplement 1 in provenance.

extraction_limitations: The LiteratureAtom model is oriented toward primary literature; this source is a systematic review/meta-analysis. Atoms therefore represent review-level methods, pooled findings, author conclusions, limitations, and companion-material assertions rather than treating underlying observational-study findings as if generated by this publication.
No attempt was made to infer unreported CCL5 thresholds, assay harmonization, patient-level covariate sets, or missing participant denominators in sensitivity analyses.
Review status remains needs_review because extraction was machine-assisted even though structural, schema, and sufficiency checks passed.
